answer.headline: ANC T12 freight is concentrated on freighters, which slightly outnumber passenger departures
answer.body:
Over {F1.period}, Ted Stevens Anchorage International (ANC) enplaned {F1} of freight ({F1.class}) and recorded {F2} passenger departures ({F2.class}). Departures of all aircraft configurations were {F3} ({F3.class}).

Freight pounds and passenger departures use different units, so the levels are not a like-for-like volume ranking. The calculated intensity is {F10} pounds of freight enplaned per passenger departure ({F1} divided by {F2}). That result is calculated from observed totals. It is not a specialization index, a forecast, or a valuation.

On a common unit, freight-configured departures were {F8} ({F8.class}) against {F2} passenger departures. Freight-configured departures exceeded passenger departures by {F16} (calculated). The ratio of freight-configured departures to passenger departures is {F11} (calculated). Freight-configured departures are {F12} of all departures (calculated); passenger departures are {F13} of all departures (calculated).

The service-type split reconciles to those totals. Passenger-configured departures were {F9} and combi departures were {F7}. Their sum is {F18}, and the difference from passenger departures is {F20} (calculated). Adding freight-configured departures gives {F19}, and the difference from all departures is {F21} (calculated). The T12 departure total is therefore fully accounted for by freight, passenger, and combi configurations.

Freight pounds by configuration, all observed: freight-configured aircraft {F5}, passenger-configured aircraft {F6}, and combi aircraft {F4}. Calculated shares of total freight enplaned are {F14}, {F15}, and {F17}. Those three shares sum to {F22}.

Within ANC over this window, dedicated freighter flying is the larger departure category and carries nearly all of the freight. Passenger departures remain large, and only a small share of freight moves on passenger aircraft. This describes the cargo-versus-passenger mix at ANC. It is not an investment screen, not a peer rank, and not evidence of unmet demand, facility capacity, fares, or profitability.

claims.text: Over {F1.period}, ANC enplaned {F1} of freight ({F1.class}) and operated {F2} passenger departures ({F2.class}) and {F3} departures of all configurations ({F3.class}).

Freight-configured departures were {F8}, passenger-configured departures were {F9}, and combi departures were {F7}. Passenger-configured plus combi departures sum to {F18}, differing from passenger departures by {F20}. All three configuration rows sum to {F19}, differing from all departures by {F21}.
Freight pounds were {F5} on freight-configured aircraft, {F6} on passenger-configured aircraft, and {F4} on combi aircraft, all observed.

Calculated comparisons are {F10} pounds of freight per passenger departure, {F11} freight-configured departures per passenger departure, a freight-configured share of all departures of {F12}, a passenger-departure share of all departures of {F13}, and an excess of freight-configured over passenger departures of {F16}.
Calculated shares of freight pounds are {F14} on freight-configured aircraft, {F15} on passenger-configured aircraft, and {F17} on combi aircraft, summing to {F22}.

Relative to its own passenger departures over this window, ANC has a cargo-weighted operating mix: freighter departures outnumber passenger departures ({F11}, excess {F16}, share of all departures {F12}), and nearly all enplaned freight is on freighter aircraft ({F14}) rather than on passenger aircraft ({F15}). The departure tilt is modest; the tonnage concentration on freighters is strong.
Why freighters dominate ANC freight — network role, geography, or carrier strategy — is not identified by these metrics. Any such cause remains a hypothesis.

assumptions: Anchorage (ANC) is bound to Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport. Merrill Field and the Anchorage CBSA as a group are excluded because the question names ANC.

Passenger departures follow the catalog definition: performed departures of passenger, combi, and seaplane aircraft. In this window that total matches passenger-configured plus combi departures (difference {F20}).

Freight-configured departures are the service-type freight slice of all departures. Cargo-versus-passenger specialization is read from that within-airport mix and from where freight pounds sit, not from a peer ranking or an investment screen.
The cross-unit comparison is freight pounds divided by passenger departures and is interpreted as pounds of freight per passenger departure.
limitations: Unmet demand, terminal or cargo-facility capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured, so this mix does not establish them.
No cross-airport rank or screen was run. Whether ANC is more cargo-specialized than other US airports is not established.
Freight enplaned excludes mail. It is segment freight on departing T-100 flights, not cargo revenue and not ton-miles.
FAA hub class for ANC is a passenger-enplanement classification and does not measure cargo specialization.
Ratios and differences are calculated from observed T12 totals. They are not forecasts or estimates.
A ratio of pounds to departures is an intensity. It does not mean freight activity is economically larger than passenger activity.
